items.evidence: After page.reload() the test asserts the note text is visible in the Order History card (e2e/tests/orders/order-notes.spec.ts:67-68). That would fail if the note mutation never ran.
All three criteria are asserted: actor "order" (line 16), the note is shown after adding it (lines 58-59), and it is still shown after reload (lines 63-68).
It reuses OrderPage.goto/statusInfo and findOrderId/ORDERS_SCENARIO. No existing page object has an order-history or note locator, so nothing is duplicated.
There is no waitForTimeout, sleep or polling loop.
It imports test/expect from ../../fixtures/test.ts, is not tagged parallel(), and does not write to the cache or the dumps.

e2e/tests/orders/order-notes.spec.ts:33-37 (diff lines 39-43): the Order History card is found by filtering every generic `div` on the page and taking `.last()`, which is a positional pick over untargeted elements instead of a test-id or role-based locator.
It opens the scenario's existing unpaid order via findOrderId. The only write is the note itself, which is the action under test.
There are no hard-coded ids. The order is looked up by scenario key, and the assertions are on the test's own note text and the scenario order's status.
It uses test.use({ actor: "order" }), the single-permission order actor. There is no UI login and no credentials.
The file is under e2e/tests/orders/ and typecheck.txt reports `exit 0: no errors`.

e2e/tests/orders/order-notes.spec.ts:29-37 (diff lines 35-43): the comment input, the Add Comment button and the history-card locators, plus the add-note action, are written inline in the spec instead of on OrderPage.
No page-object members were added, so this does not apply.
It has // Arrange, // Act and // Assert comments (lines 24, 46, 52).
e2e/tests/orders/order-notes.spec.ts:39-68 (diff lines 45-74): opening the order, adding the note and reloading are separate stages in one test with no test.step.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e (line 21).
A header block comment (lines 10-14) says what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first expect(locator) calls.
The scenario name is the imported ORDERS_SCENARIO and no money is compared. The status literal matches suite practice.
e2e/tests/orders/order-notes.spec.ts:26 (diff line 32): the note text gets a randomUUID suffix to make it unique, which is unnecessary because the database is reset before each test.
There are no per-test timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState calls.
Relative imports keep .ts, and test/expect come only from the fixture.
There is no any, no cast and no gql call.

e2e/tests/orders/order-notes.spec.ts:15,25,39,47,63 (diff lines 21,31,45,53,69): numbered generated step comments such as "// 3. Open the order" and "// 5. Fill the Comment textbox ... and click Add Comment" restate the next line instead of explaining why.

structured_output.summary: The spec runs as the order-only actor on the scenario's unpaid order and proves the note persists by checking it again after a reload, so B1 and B2 are met and it type-checks. The one blocker is B6: the Order History card is located by filtering every div and taking `.last()`. Four minors fail: M1, because the locators and the add-note action sit inline in the spec instead of on OrderPage; M4, because the stages have no test.step; M9, because the note text is made unique with randomUUID; and M13, because the numbered step comments narrate the code.
